ModMetaData.name: Insects Aren't Raiders
ModMetaData.author: tk421storm
ModMetaData.description:
In vanilla, hive insects switch to the same "assault the colony" behavior raiders use, and it doesn't take much: a wildfire, a mortar shell, a raid by another faction or a destroyed hive can send a whole swarm marching across the map to attack anything of yours. With this mod they act like animals defending a nest.

 - Hives only attack when their insects saw a colonist attack them: a shot, a melee hit or a thrown molotov from someone within sight. Fires (even ones you started), mortars, turrets, traps, heat and other factions make the hive defend itself aggressively instead, fighting what it can see within about 40 cells of the hive.
 - Insects that do attack move as a swarm: they follow a point that moves toward their target, fight what they see around it, and nibble at walls in their way rather than breaching. A hive's swarm goes home once it has nothing left to chase; insect ambushes and other insect raids keep hunting.
 - A hive defending itself is easy to spot: its insects run patrols across most of that area instead of walking around the hive.
 - Insects whose hive is destroyed keep defending the spot where it stood. After 3 to 4 days the survivors become wild insects that wander, hunt and leave the map like other wild animals.
 - Insects from disturbed cocoons come out as enraged wild insects that attack what they can see nearby for a few hours, then calm down.

Applies to all hives, infestations included. Insect lair maps are unchanged.
